Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:10:1.english: And it is taught - [This is stated] in a calm tone [i.e., as an assertion, not a question].

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:13:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דאם לא נתן לה בתוך ל', אינה מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:13:1.english: [It is] obvious - That if he did not give [it] to her within thirty [days], she is not betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:13:2.hebrew: לאו תנאה הוא - ולא קפדה אשלשים יום, אלא לזרוזיה בעלמא קאמרה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:13:2.english: It is not a condition - And she was not particular about the thirty days; rather, she said [it] merely to urge him on.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:14:1.hebrew: ויש לו - משמע שיש עדים שיש לו, הא לאו הכי — אינה מקודשת ומותרת לאחר. ואמאי? ניחוש שמא יש לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:14:1.english: And he has [it] - [This] implies that there are witnesses that he has [it]; for if not so, she is not betrothed and is permitted to another. But why? Let us be concerned that perhaps he has [it]!

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:15:1.hebrew: קידושי ודאי הוו - אם אנו יודעים שיש לו, ונפקא מינה שאם בא אחר וקידשה — אינה מקודשת. וכי לא ידעינן — חיישינן שמא יש לו, ואינה מותרת לאחר; ומיהו, צריכה גט מן השני, דשמא לא היו הראשונים קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:15:1.english: They are a definite betrothal - If we know that he has [it]; and the practical difference is that if another [man] came and betrothed her, she is not betrothed [to him]. And when we do not know, we are concerned lest he has [it], and she is not permitted to another; however, she requires a bill of divorce from the second [as well], lest the first [act] was not a [valid] betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:16:1.hebrew: לא נתכוונה זו אלא לראות משלו - לפיכך, אם הראה על השלחן שלפניו, והוא שולחני והמעות אינם שלו — אינה מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:16:1.english: This woman intended only to see [money] of his own - Therefore, if he showed [her] on the table before him, and he is a moneychanger and the coins are not his — she is not betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:16:2.hebrew: בעיסקא - למחצית שכר, היו לפניו על שולחנו להחליף ולהשתכר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:16:2.english: As a joint venture - [Entrusted to him] for half the profit; [the coins] were before him on his table to exchange and earn a profit.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:17:1.hebrew: בית כור - מקום הראוי לזרוע ל' סאין. וחשבינן לכל סאתים מאה על חמשים כחצר המשכן — חמשים על חמשים לבית סאה; ובית כור: אלף ות"ק אורך על נ' רוחב. ואם אתה מרבעו — תמצאנו מאתים ושבעים ושלשה וה' טפחים על מאתים ושבעים ושלשה וה' טפחים, ועוד דבר מועט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:17:1.english: A beit kor - An area suitable for sowing thirty se'ah [of seed]. And we calculate for every two se'ah [an area of] one hundred by fifty [cubits], like the Courtyard of the Tabernacle — fifty by fifty [cubits] for a beit se'ah; and [thus] a beit kor [is] one thousand and five hundred [cubits] in length by fifty [cubits] in width. And if you make it square, you will find it [to be] two hundred and seventy-three [cubits] and five handbreadths by two hundred and seventy-three [cubits] and five handbreadths, and a small amount more.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:17:2.hebrew: ויש לו - משמע שיש עדים שיש לו, הא לאו הכי — אינה מקודשת ומותרת לאחר. ואמאי? ניחוש שמא יש לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:17:2.english: And he possesses [it] - This implies that there are witnesses that he possesses [it]; for otherwise, she is not betrothed and is permitted to [marry] another [man]. And why? Let us be concerned that perhaps he possesses [it]!

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:17:3.hebrew: ואם הראה בבקעה - ״הרי ליך בקעה גדולה ובה כמה בתי כורין״, ואין אחד מהן שלו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:17:3.english: And if he showed [her land] in a valley - [Saying:] “Here before you is a large valley, and in it are several batei kor,” yet not one of them is his.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:19:1.hebrew: זוזי הוא דעבידי אינשי דמצנעי - והתם הוא דחזינא: אי יש לו — הוו קידושי ודאי; לא חזינא — הוו קידושי ספק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:19:1.english: It is money that people tend to hide - And it is there that we see: if he has [it], it is a definite betrothal; [if] we do not see [it], it is an uncertain betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:19:2.hebrew: אבל ארעא - אי לא ידעינן דיש לו, אפילו קידושי ספק ליכא, דמאן דאית ליה ארעא — קלא אית ליה. קמ"ל — מדתננהו גבי הדדי — למימרא דארעא כי זוזי: מה התם יש לו — ודאי, אין לו — ספק; אף קרקע: יש לו — ודאי, אין לו — ספק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:19:2.english: But [with regard to] land - If we do not know that he has [land], there is not even an uncertain betrothal, for whoever has land, it generates publicity. [The mishna] teaches us — from [the fact] that they were taught alongside one another — to say that land is like money: Just as there, [if] he has [money, it is a] definite [betrothal, and if] he does not have [known money, it is an] uncertain [betrothal]; so too [with] land: [if] he has [it, it is a] definite [betrothal], [and if] he does not have [known land, it is an] uncertain [betrothal].

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:1:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - על כרחיך, לרב הונא נמי אסורה לינשא עד שתתן, שמא לא יתקיים התנאי, וגט בטל, ובניה ממזרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:1:1.english: What is [the difference] between them - Of necessity, according to Rav Huna as well she is forbidden to marry until she gives [the money], lest the condition not be fulfilled, and the bill of divorce [be] void, and her children [be] mamzerim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:20:1.hebrew: מאי נפק' ליך מינה - אם רחוק הוא, אנא טרחנא ומייתינא התבואה לביתי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:20:1.english: What difference does it make to you - If it is far, I will take the trouble and bring the produce to my house.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:21:1.hebrew: אבל לכ"ע תנאה הוי - ואפילו ת"ק מודה, שאם פירש "על מנת שתתן לי או ליורשיי", שאפילו מת — נותנה ליורשיו, ופטורה מן החליצה, דהוה ליה גט למפרע משקבלתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:21:1.english: But according to everyone, it is a condition - And even the first tanna concedes that if he had specified, “on the condition that you give [it] to me or to my heirs,” that even if he died, she gives it to his heirs and is exempt from chalitzah, as it is a bill of divorce retroactively from [the time] that she received it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:21:2.hebrew: לא נתכוונה זו אלא לראות משלו - לפיכך, אם הראה על השלחן שלפניו והוא שולחני והמעות אינם שלו — אינה מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:21:2.english: This [woman] intended only to see [property] of his own - Therefore, if he showed [her money] on the table before him, and he is a money changer and the coins are not his, she is not betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:2:1.hebrew: דלקרובה אתי - ומיהר לקרבה אליו, וגמר קידושין בפרוטה שנתן לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:2:1.english: Because he comes to draw her near - And [so] he hastened to draw her near to him, and concluded the betrothal with the peruta that he gave her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:2:2.hebrew: אימא מודה ליה לרב יהודה - דלא גמר למיהוי גיטא עד שתתן, אולי יתפייסו בינתיים, שאין אדם ממהר לרחק את אשתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:2:2.english: Say [that] he concedes to Rav Yehuda - That he does not fully resolve for it to be a bill of divorce until she gives [the money], [thinking that] perhaps they will reconcile in the meantime, for a person does not hasten to distance his wife.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:3:1.hebrew: בהך קאמר רב הונא - דמגורשת מיד, לא חשש הבעל לעכב גירושיה עד שיקבל המעות, משום דלא כסיף למתבע לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:3:1.english: In this [case] Rav Huna says - That she is divorced immediately — the husband was not concerned to delay her divorce until he receives the money, because he is not ashamed to demand [it] from her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:3:2.english: Say that he concedes to Rav Yehuda - For she did not consent to her betrothal until he gives [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:4:1.english: Was torn - Before she gave [the money].

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:5:1.english: [If] she gave - Before he died.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:6:1.hebrew: אבל לכ"ע תנאה הוי - ואפילו ת"ק מודה, שאם פירש "על מנת שתתן לי או ליורשיי", שאפילו מת — נותנה ליורשיו, ופטורה מן החליצה, דהוה ליה גט למפרע משקבלתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:6:1.english: However, according to everyone, it is a condition - And even the first tanna concedes that if he explicitly stated: “On the condition that you give [it] to me or to my heirs,” that even if he died, she gives it to his heirs and is exempt from chalitzah, as it is a bill of divorce retroactively from [the moment] she received it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:7:1.hebrew: כאומר מעכשיו - ע"מ כך וכך דמי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:7:1.english: Like one who says: "From now" - It is considered like [saying: "...from now,] on condition of such-and-such."

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:9:1.english: When I ascended to there - When I ascended to the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:9:2.hebrew: לא נחלקו - כלומר, לא מספקא להו לרבנן אי תנאה אי חזרה, אלא במהיום ולאחר מיתה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 60b:9:2.english: They did not disagree - That is to say, the Rabbis were not in doubt whether [it is] a condition or a retraction, except regarding "from today and after death."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 60b:1:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו שנתקרע הגט או שנאבד - ולא רצה לשנויי: איכא בינייהו דפשטה ידה וקבלה קידושין מאחר כדלעיל, דא"כ היה צריך לומר: דלרב הונא צריכה גט משני, ולרב יהודה אינה צריכה גט משני. והא ליתא, דהא אפילו לרב יהודה נמי צריכה גט מספק, [כדפר"י] פרק מי שאחזו (גיטין עד.) לכשתתן, דמגורשת ואינה מגורשת עד שתתן. ולעיל נמי גבי קידושין, לא מצי לשנויי: איכא בינייהו שנאבדו הקידושין שנתן לה בשעת קידושין, כדמשני הכא גבי גיטין שנאבד הגט, והכי נפרש לעיל: לרב הונא הוו קידושין ולרב יהודה לא הוו קידושין — דהא לכ"ע אפילו נתאכלו המעות הוו קידושין, כיון דבתורת קידושין יהבינהו, כדאמרינן בפרקין (לעיל קידושין דף נט.): האומר לאשה הרי את מקודשת לי לאחר ל' יום, מקודשת אפילו נתאכלו המעות:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 60b:1:1.english: The difference between them is where the bill of divorce was torn or lost - And [the Gemara] did not want to answer that the difference between them is where she extended her hand and accepted betrothal from another [man], as [it answered] above, for if so, it would have had to say that according to Rav Huna she requires a bill of divorce from the second [husband], and according to Rav Yehuda she does not require a bill of divorce from the second. But this is not so, for even according to Rav Yehuda she also requires a bill of divorce out of doubt, [as the Ri explained] in the chapter [entitled] Mi She’aḥazo (Gittin 74a) regarding "when she gives," that she is [in the status of] divorced and not divorced until she gives [it]. And above as well, regarding betrothal, [the Gemara] could not answer that the difference between them is that the betrothal [money] that he gave her at the time of betrothal was lost, as it answers here regarding divorce where the bill of divorce was lost, and so we would explain above: according to Rav Huna it is a valid betrothal, and according to Rav Yehuda it is not a valid betrothal; for according to all, even if the money was consumed it is a valid betrothal, since he gave them as betrothal [money], as we say in our chapter (above, Kiddushin 59a): One who says to a woman, "Behold, you are betrothed to me after thirty days," she is betrothed even if the money was consumed.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 60b:6:1.hebrew: אבל דכ"ע תנאה הוי - פירוש: ואפילו ת"ק מודה, שאם פירש "ע"מ שתתני לי או ליורשיי", שאפי' מת נותנת ליורשים ופטורה מן החליצה, דהוה ליה גיטא למפרע משקבלתו. ותיובתא דרב יהודה, דאמר לעיל "לכשתתן", דלדידיה לא הוי גט; דהא לכי יהבה ליה הוי גיטא, והשתא מיהא לא הוי גיטא, דאין גט לאחר מיתה. ואם תאמר: מאי מקשה לרב יהודה? דלמא דכ"ע סברי "לי ואפילו ליורשיי", ובהא פליגי בין ת"ק לרשב"ג: דת"ק סבר כרב יהודה, דאמר "לכשתתן" ולא הוי גט, ורשב"ג סבר כרב הונא, ומש"ה קאמר דנותנת ליורשים, שהגט חל עליה למפרע? וי"ל, דמשמע ליה לגמרא דהלשון דקאמר "לא נתנה זקוקה ליבם", ר"ל דמתייבמת אם תרצה. ולרב יהודה, מגורשת מיהא מספק למפרע, כדפירשתי לעיל: לכשתתן מגורשת ואינה מגורשת עד שתתן; וא"כ הוי ספיקא של אשת אחיו שלא במקום מצוה, שהרי אם תתננה לאחד מן הקרובים מגורשת מספק למפרע, ואם כן כיון דספיקא הוא — חולצת ולא מתייבמת. ומהכא הוי ראיה למאי דפרישית לעיל: דלרב יהודה דאמר לכשתתן — הוי גט ואינו גט עד שתתן; דאם לא כן, לישני הכא נמי דקאי כת"ק:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 60b:6:1.english: "However, everyone agrees that it is a condition" - Explanation: Even the first tanna concedes that if he had explicitly stated, "On the condition that you will give [the money] to me or to my heirs," that even if he died, she gives [it] to the heirs and is exempt from chalitzah, as it is a [valid] bill of divorce retroactively from [the moment] she received it. And [this is] a refutation of Rav Yehuda, who said above [that "on the condition" means] "when she gives," for according to his [view] it would not be a bill of divorce; for [according to him] only when she gives it to him does it become a bill of divorce, and now [at the time of delivery], at any rate, it is not a bill of divorce, and there is no divorce after death. And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] raise an objection against Rav Yehuda? Perhaps everyone holds [that "to me" means] "to me and even to my heirs," and this is what the first tanna and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagree about: the first tanna holds like Rav Yehuda, who said [that it means] "when she gives," and [therefore once he dies] it is not a bill of divorce; while Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds like Rav Huna, and for that reason he says that she gives [it] to the heirs, since the bill of divorce takes effect upon her retroactively? And one can say: The Gemara understood that the phrasing which says: "If she did not give, she is bound to the yavam," means that she enters into levirate marriage if she wishes. Whereas according to Rav Yehuda, she is at any rate divorced out of doubt retroactively, as I explained above: [when one says] "when she gives," she is [in the status of] divorced and not divorced until she gives; and if so, [permitting her to enter into levirate marriage] would be a situation of doubt regarding a brother's wife where there is no mitzvah [i.e., a forbidden union], for if she were to give [the money] to one of the relatives, she would be divorced out of doubt retroactively. And if so, since it is a matter of doubt, she must perform chalitzah and may not enter into levirate marriage. And from here there is proof for what I explained above: that according to Rav Yehuda, who said "when she gives," it is a bill of divorce and not a bill of divorce until she gives; for if this were not so, let [the Gemara] answer here as well that [Rav Yehuda] stands in accordance with the first tanna.
